mainTopic: Lending with רבית to non-Jews, priority in lending, and רבי's puzzle about a גר and a גר תושב
overview: This amud begins by finishing an answer: lending with רבית to a non-Jew is allowed only as much as one needs to make a living. רבינא gives another answer: the משנה is about תלמידי חכמים, who will not learn from the non-Jew's ways. Another version places רב הונא's teaching on רב יוסף's ברייתא about who comes first for a loan. A Jew comes first even if the גוי would pay רבית. Next come strong words against lending with רבית, and a promise that the honest lender may fall but will rise again. The גמרא then works through רבי's puzzle about a גר in the sale of a slave. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that a גר can buy an עבד עברי only under the rules of a gentile owner. Along the way, the גמרא explains why a woman may not buy an עבד עברי, and why a widow may not raise a dog. Finally, 'מאתו' shows that the ban on רבית covers only a Jew, so it is allowed with a גר תושב, and a person may be a guarantor for a loan with interest.

steps.title: Finishing the earlier answer: only enough to make a living
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier answer: the permission to lend with רבית to a non-Jew is limited to what one needs to live on.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It is only permitted] to the extent needed for his livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish an answer that started just before this point. That answer said lending with רבית to a non-Jew is allowed only as much as a person needs to make a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן made a decree against lending to non-Jews with רבית, yet the משנה allows it. This answer settles the clash by saying the משנה only allows it in a limited amount, enough to live on. It must not become a regular business.

keyTerms.meaning: To the extent needed for his livelihood
A non-Jew who lives in the Jewish land and keeps the seven Noahide laws

phrases.english: To the extent of his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּכְדֵי חַיָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer that began before this section, resolving the clash between the decree and the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the permission covers only a small amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to allow lending to non-Jews with רבית without any limit, against the רבנן's decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is allowed only as much as one needs for a livelihood.

steps.title: Another answer: the משנה is talking about Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה is about תלמידי חכמים. The decree exists so a person won't learn from the non-Jew's ways, and a תלמיד חכם won't learn from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Here we are dealing with Torah scholars. What is the reason the רבנן made the decree? So that he should not learn from the non-Jew's actions. Since this lender is a Torah scholar, he will not learn from his actions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different way to explain why the משנה allows lending with רבית to a non-Jew, even though the רבנן decreed against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא looks at the reason behind the decree: too much business contact might lead a Jew to copy the non-Jew's behavior. A תלמיד חכם is not at risk of that, so the decree does not apply to him. The decree still stands. רבינא is only describing who it does not reach.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (the case under discussion)
Perhaps he will learn from his actions

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא using the reason behind a rabbinic decree to decide which people the decree covers.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Here we are dealing with Torah scholars.
What is the reason the Rabbis decreed?
Perhaps he will learn from his actions,
phrases.notes: "His" here means the non-Jewish borrower.

phrases.english: and since he is a Torah scholar,
he will not learn from his actions.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same difficulty that step 1 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to certain people, based on the reason for the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree should forbid anyone from lending to a non-Jew with רבית, so the משנה is hard to understand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a תלמיד חכם, who is not at risk of learning bad ways, so the reason for the decree does not apply to him.

steps.title: Another version: רב יוסף's teaching on who comes first in lending
steps.stepSummary: Some placed רב הונא's teaching on רב יוסף's ברייתא. The ברייתא lists the order of priority for loans: a Jew before a גוי, a poor person before a rich one, relatives before townspeople, and townspeople before people from other towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רב הונא's statement on what רב יוסף taught: "If you lend money to My people, to the poor person with you." My people and a גוי: My people come first. A poor person and a rich person: the poor person comes first. Your own poor and the poor of your city: your own poor come first. The poor of your city and the poor of another city: the poor of your city come first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a different version of where רב הונא's teaching was said. It first quotes רב יוסף's ברייתא about the order of priority when lending money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads each word of the פסוק as a priority rule. "עמי" puts a Jew before a גוי, "העני" puts a poor person before a rich one, and "עמך" puts those closest to you first. רב הונא's actual teaching comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)

steps.whatToRemember: Order of priority for loans: a Jew before a גוי, poor before rich, your relatives before your townspeople, your townspeople before people from another town.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: There are those who teach this statement of Rav Huna
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's teaching that the גמרא brought earlier. This version ties it to a different source.

phrases.english: on that which Rav Yosef taught:
"If you lend money to My people,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:24

phrases.english: to the poor person with you."
My people and a gentile: My people come first,
a poor person and a rich person: the poor person comes first.
"Your poor and the poor of your city": your poor come first,
phrases.notes: "Your poor" means your own poor relatives.

phrases.english: the poor of your city and the poor of another city:
the poor of your city come first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא אַהָא דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבית question and brings another version of where רב הונא's teaching belongs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When lending money, those closer to you come first: a Jew before a גוי, poor before rich, relatives before townspeople, townspeople before outsiders.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that a Jew comes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first rule of the ברייתא and asks why it needs to be said, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: My people and a גוי, My people come first. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and challenges it as פשיטא, something too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody would think a גוי gets priority over a fellow Jew for a loan. So the גמרא asks what this rule adds. This question sets up רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting a line from the ברייתא just cited)

phrases.english: The Master said:
My people and a gentile, My people come first.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: עַמִּי וְגוֹי עַמִּי קוֹדֵם, פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first rule of the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a Jew comes before a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems so obvious that the ברייתא should not need to say it.

steps.title: A Jew comes first even when the גוי would pay interest
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the rule teaches something new: a Jew comes first even if you could lend to the גוי with רבית and must lend to the Jew for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me: It is needed only to teach that even if one could lend to a גוי with interest and to a Jew for free, the Jew still comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reports רב הונא's answer to the question of פשיטא. The rule is needed for the case where lending to the Jew means giving up profit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With equal terms, the Jew coming first would be obvious. The new point is that you must prefer the Jew even when you lose money by doing so. That is רב הונא's teaching, which this version places on רב יוסף's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only (to teach a special case)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew comes first for a loan even if you would earn רבית from the גוי and nothing from the Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule: helping a fellow Jew comes before making a profit.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna told me:
phrases.notes: "הונא" is רב הונא, the same person whose teaching the גמרא mentioned in step 3.

phrases.english: It is necessary only
for when, even to a gentile with interest
and to a Jew for free [the Jew comes first].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לִי הוּנָא: לָא נִצְרְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of פשיטא from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the rule's new point in a less obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule that a Jew comes first seems obvious and unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a Jew comes first even when lending to him means giving up רבית from a גוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Priority goes to the Jew even at a financial loss to the lender.

steps.title: The blindness of those who lend with interest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי points out that a lender who charges רבית signs a document that amounts to saying he denies God.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי said: Come and see how blind people who lend with interest are. If one person calls another 'wicked,' the other fights him with his whole life. But these lenders bring witnesses, a scribe, a pen and ink, and they write and sign: 'This person has denied the God of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing how terrible lending with רבית is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People get furious when someone calls them 'wicked' out loud. Yet a lender who charges רבית writes a signed, witnessed document that shows he ignores the Torah. רבי יוסי calls this blindness, because the lender doesn't see that he is shaming himself in writing.

keyTerms.meaning: Blindness of the eyes; not seeing what you are really doing

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei said:
Come and see the blindness of the eyes
of those who lend with interest.
If a person calls his fellow "wicked,"
the other goes after his very life.
phrases.notes: He means the insulted person fights back and makes his life hard in every way.

phrases.english: But they bring witnesses and a scribe
and a pen and ink,
and they write and sign:
This so-and-so has denied the God of Israel.
phrases.notes: The loan document with interest works like a signed statement that he ignores God's Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בֹּא וּרְאֵה סַמְיוּת עֵינֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of who to lend to first, the גמרא brings teachings about how serious רבית is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lending with רבית is like signing a document saying one denies the God of Israel.

steps.title: Lending without interest keeps one from falling
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies a פסוק in תהלים to one who lends without רבית, and learns that one who lends with רבית will see his property collapse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Anyone who has money and lends it without interest, the פסוק says about him: 'He did not give his money with interest, and did not take a bribe against the innocent; one who does these will never fall.' So you learn that anyone who lends with interest, his property collapses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that promises stability to one who lends without רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the honest lender 'will never fall.' רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads the opposite from it: one who lends with רבית will fall, meaning his property will collapse.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Anyone who has money
and lends it without interest,
about him the פסוק says:
"He did not give his money with interest,
phrases.notes: תהלים 15:5

phrases.english: and did not take a bribe against the innocent;
one who does these will never fall."
So you have learned that anyone who lends with interest,
his property collapses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same theme of how serious רבית is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who lends without רבית will not fall; one who lends with רבית will see his property collapse.

steps.title: But honest lenders also lose their money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that we see people who do not lend with רבית whose property still collapses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see people who do not lend with interest, and their property still collapses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's promise using what we see in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promised that the honest lender 'will never fall.' Yet real life shows honest people losing their wealth too, so the promise seems not to hold.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּלָא מוֹזְפִי בְּרִבִּית
phrases.english: But we see people who do not lend with interest
and still their property collapses!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּלָא מוֹזְפִי בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the promise made in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that one who lends without רבית 'will never fall.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real life shows honest lenders whose property collapses, which seems to go against the פסוק.

steps.title: Honest people fall but rise again
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that honest lenders may fall but then recover, while those who lend with רבית fall and do not recover.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: These fall and rise again, and those fall and do not rise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge by explaining what 'never fall' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Never fall' doesn't mean nothing bad ever happens. It means the fall is not permanent. The honest lender recovers, but the one who lends with רבית stays down.
steps.whatToRemember: Lending without רבית does not promise that one will never lose money. It promises that any loss will be temporary, unlike the lasting loss of one who lends with רבית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
These collapse and rise again,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the people who lend without interest.

phrases.english: and those collapse and do not rise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַלָּלוּ מִתְמוֹטְטִין וְעוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק promises that the honest lender will never lose money at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The honest lender may fall, but he will rise again; the one who lends with רבית falls for good.

steps.title: The wicked can only swallow a partly righteous person
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains a פסוק in חבקוק: the wicked can swallow someone only 'more righteous than he,' but not a completely righteous person.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Why do You look on at the treacherous, and stay silent when the wicked swallows one more righteous than he?' רב הונא said: One who is only more righteous than him, the wicked can swallow. A completely righteous person, he cannot swallow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching about why good people sometimes suffer at the hands of the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to complain that the wicked can harm the righteous. רב הונא reads the words carefully: it says 'more righteous than he,' meaning only somewhat better than the wicked person. A fully righteous person is protected.

phrases.english: "Why do You look on at the treacherous,
phrases.notes: חבקוק 1:13

phrases.english: and stay silent when the wicked swallows
one more righteous than he?"
Rav Huna said:
One more righteous than him, he swallows;
a completely righteous person, he does not swallow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה תַבִּיט בּוֹגְדִים תַּחֲרִישׁ כְּבַלַּע רָשָׁע צַדִּיק מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 9, that good people may suffer for a time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wicked can harm someone only somewhat more righteous than he, but not a completely righteous person.

steps.title: רבי is puzzled by גר צדק and גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה, a ברייתא brings רבי saying he does not understand the mention of a גר צדק regarding a sale and a גר תושב regarding רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי says: The righteous convert mentioned regarding a sale, and the resident non-Jew mentioned regarding interest, I do not know what they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's mention of a גר תושב and sets up a question that it will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי points to two places in the Torah where these terms appear, and he says he does not understand them. This is an opening line; the גמרא will now work out what bothered him.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous convert, a full convert to Judaism
A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who keeps the seven מצוות of בני נח
A sale (here, selling oneself as a slave)

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi says:
The righteous convert mentioned regarding a sale,
phrases.notes: This refers to a Jew who sells himself as a slave.

phrases.english: and the resident non-Jew mentioned regarding interest,
I do not know what it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: גֵּר צֶדֶק הָאָמוּר לְעִנְיַן מְכִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side teachings and goes back to explaining the משנה's mention of a גר תושב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי says he does not understand the Torah's mention of a גר צדק regarding a sale and a גר תושב regarding רבית.

steps.title: The source for a sale to a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the גר צדק 'mentioned regarding a sale': a ברייתא learns from ויקרא 25 that a poor Jew may be sold to a גר, a גר תושב, a gentile, and even to idol worship itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The righteous convert mentioned regarding a sale comes from this source. It is written: 'If your brother becomes poor with you and is sold to you.' The ברייתא learns: not only to you, but even to a convert, as it says 'to a stranger.' And not only to a righteous convert, but even to a גר תושב, as it says 'to a stranger who is a settler.' 'A stranger's family' means a gentile. When it says 'or to an offshoot,' it means one who is sold to idol worship itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing which source רבי meant when he spoke of a גר צדק regarding a sale. It brings a ברייתא that explains, word by word, who a poor Jew may end up being sold to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word in the פסוק adds a lower level that the poor Jew might sink to: first a גר, then a גר תושב, then a gentile, and finally service for idol worship itself. The key point for our סוגיא is the first step. The פסוק seems to say that a גר צדק can buy a Hebrew slave.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who accepted the seven Noahide laws and lives in the land
Sale; here, a poor Jew selling himself as a slave
Offshoot; read here as service of idol worship

phrases.english: The righteous convert mentioned regarding a sale:
as it is written: "If your brother becomes poor with you
and is sold to you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:39

phrases.english: And not only to you, but even to a convert,
as it says: "to a stranger."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לְגֵר צֶדֶק אֶלָּא לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב,
phrases.english: And not only to a righteous convert, but even to a resident non-Jew,
as it says: "to a stranger who is a settler."
"A stranger's family": this is the gentile.
When it says "or to an offshoot"
this is one who is sold to idol worship itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר צֶדֶק הָאָמוּר לְעִנְיַן מְכִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source behind רבי's mention of a גר צדק regarding a sale.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reference is to the ברייתא that learns from 'לגר' that a poor Jew may be sold to a convert.

steps.title: Can a convert really buy a Hebrew slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that a Jew may be sold to a גר, citing another ברייתא that says a גר can neither be bought as an עבד עברי nor buy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Not only to you, but even to a convert, as it says to a stranger.' Does this mean a convert can acquire a Hebrew slave? But compare this other ברייתא: A convert cannot be acquired as a Hebrew slave, and a woman and a convert cannot acquire a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא again and asks whether it really means a גר can own an עבד עברי. It then brings another ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא reads 'לגר' to mean a Jew can be sold to a convert. The second ברייתא clearly says a גר cannot acquire an עבד עברי. The two sources seem to contradict each other, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; introduces a closer look at a line from a ברייתא just quoted
Is this to say...?; draws out what a statement implies
And contrast it with; brings a source that contradicts

phrases.english: The Master said:
"And not only to you, but even to a convert,
as it says: 'to a stranger.'"
Is this to say that a convert can acquire a Hebrew slave?
But contrast it with this:
A convert cannot be acquired as a Hebrew slave,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה וְגֵר קוֹנִין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי.
phrases.english: and a woman and a convert cannot acquire a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּגֵר קָנֵי עֶבֶד עִבְרִי? ורְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first line of the ברייתא from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of 'לגר' as permitting a sale to a convert.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two ברייתות: one says a Jew may be sold to a גר, the other says a גר cannot acquire an עבד עברי.

steps.title: Why a convert cannot be sold as a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first rule of the contradicting ברייתא: an עבד עברי must 'return to his family' when freed, and a גר has no such family.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert cannot be acquired as a Hebrew slave, because we need the condition 'and he shall return to his family,' and here that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the reason for the first rule in the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes a freed עבד עברי as returning to his family. A convert has no family in this sense, so he does not fit the פסוק. Therefore he cannot become an עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall return to his family (ויקרא 25:41)
It is not there; it is missing

phrases.english: A convert cannot be acquired as a Hebrew slave:
we require "and he shall return to his family,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:41

phrases.english: and that is missing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר לֹא נִקְנֶה בְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first clause of the ברייתא quoted in the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר cannot become an עבד עברי, because he cannot fulfill 'ושב אל משפחתו.'

steps.title: Why a woman or a convert cannot buy a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the second rule: a woman may not buy an עבד עברי because it is improper, and a גר may not because of a tradition that only one who can be acquired can acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman and a convert cannot acquire a Hebrew slave. A woman, because it is not proper conduct. A convert, because we have a tradition: one who can be acquired can acquire, and one who cannot be acquired cannot acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second rule of the ברייתא, giving a separate reason for the woman and for the convert. This sharpens the challenge from step 13, which step 16 answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, the reason is about proper behavior. For a גר, it ties back to step 14: since he cannot be bought as an עבד עברי, the tradition says he cannot buy one either. This makes the contradiction with the ברייתא of step 12 even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper conduct; the right way to behave
One who can be acquired can acquire

steps.confusionAlert: Step 15 only explains the contradicting ברייתא. It does not answer the קשיא from step 13. The next step, step 16, answers it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה וְגֵר קוֹנִין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי:
phrases.english: And a woman and a convert cannot acquire a Hebrew slave:
A woman: it is not proper conduct.
A convert, too: we have a tradition:
one who can be acquired can acquire,
one who cannot be acquired cannot acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה וְגֵר קוֹנִין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second clause of the contradicting ברייתא, building on step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman cannot buy an עבד עברי because it is improper. A גר cannot buy one because only one who can be acquired as an עבד עברי can acquire one.

steps.title: A גר can buy an עבד עברי, but only under the rules of a gentile owner
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק resolves the contradiction. A גר cannot buy an עבד עברי with the rules of a Jewish owner, but he can buy one with the rules of a gentile owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He cannot buy with his status being like a Jewish owner, but he can buy with his status being like a gentile owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 13. One ברייתא lets a Jew be sold to a גר, while another says a גר cannot buy an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק says both ברייתות are right, because they mean different kinds of 'buying.' The ברייתא that says 'he cannot buy' means he cannot own the slave under the full rules of a Jewish owner. The ברייתא that allows the sale means he can own the slave under the rules that apply to a gentile owner.

keyTerms.meaning: His law, meaning which set of rules applies to him
Like a Jew, under the rules of a Jewish owner
Like a gentile, under the rules of a gentile owner

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not saying the slave stops being an עבד עברי. He is saying which set of owner-rules applies to the גר who bought him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer settles רבי's question from step 11. It explains why a גר can show up in the פסוק about selling a Jew, even though a גר normally cannot buy an עבד עברי.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
He cannot acquire with his law being like a Jew's,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the גר from the two ברייתות in steps 12 and 13.

phrases.english: but he can acquire with his law being like a gentile's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֵינוֹ קוֹנֶה וְדִינוֹ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 13, after steps 14 and 15 explained the second ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two kinds of acquisition (two different legal statuses)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly argue: one allows a גר to buy an עבד עברי and the other forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גר cannot buy under the rules of a Jewish owner, but he can buy under the rules of a gentile owner.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows what 'like a gentile owner' means
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a slave whose ear was pierced, and a slave sold to a gentile, do not go on serving the master's son or daughter. This shows the special rule that applies to a gentile owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: One whose ear was pierced, and one who was sold to a gentile, does not serve the son and does not serve the daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support and explain רב נחמן בר יצחק. It shows one practical difference between a Jewish owner and a gentile owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under a Jewish owner, an עבד עברי who still has time left on his six years keeps serving the owner's son after the owner dies. A slave sold to a gentile does not pass on to the owner's children, and neither does a נרצע. A גר who buys an עבד עברי follows this gentile rule, so when the גר dies, the slave goes free.

keyTerms.meaning: An עבד עברי whose ear was pierced because he chose to stay a slave after six years
A Jew who was sold as a slave to a gentile
As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: One whose ear was pierced, and one who was sold to a gentile,
does not serve the son,
and not the daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַנִּרְצָע וְהַנִּמְכָּר לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק by showing that a separate set of rules exists for a gentile owner.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's idea that a גר can own an עבד עברי under the rules of a gentile owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a נרצע and one sold to a gentile do not serve the master's son or daughter.

steps.title: Does 'a woman cannot buy an עבד עברי' go against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that a woman and a גר cannot buy an עבד עברי. It suggests this goes against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows a woman to buy male slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A woman and a גר do not acquire an עבד עברי. Shall we say this is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? For it is taught: A woman may acquire maidservants but may not acquire male slaves. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: She may also acquire male slaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 13 and looks at its rule about a woman. It asks whether that rule fits only the רבנן and not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the other ברייתא says a woman may not buy male slaves, because of צניעות. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it. So it looks like our ברייתא, which forbids a woman to buy an עבד עברי, follows only the first opinion and goes against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said,' the formula for quoting a line from a ברייתא already cited
Shall we say, the formula for suggesting a possible conclusion
A תנא who argues here and allows a woman to buy male slaves

phrases.english: The Master said: And a woman and a convert do not
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא brought in step 13.

phrases.english: acquire a Hebrew slave.

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: Shall we say it is not in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
As it is taught: A woman may acquire maidservants,
but she may not acquire male slaves.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She may also acquire male slaves!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה וְגֵר קוֹנִין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי. נֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the גר and goes back to the woman's rule in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a woman cannot buy an עבד עברי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets a woman buy male slaves, so the ברייתא seems to follow only the opposing opinion.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was speaking only about an עבד כנעני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל too. The ברייתא forbids an עבד עברי, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows only an עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and there is no difficulty: here it is about an עבד עברי, there it is about an עבד כנעני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 18. It shows that the two sources are talking about different kinds of slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא, which says a woman cannot buy, is talking about an עבד עברי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows her to buy, is talking about an עבד כנעני. So even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that a woman may not buy an עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say, the formula for showing that a source can fit even the opinion that seemed to oppose it
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
it is not difficult:
Here, it is about a Hebrew slave,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our ברייתא, which forbids a woman to buy.

phrases.english: there, it is about a Canaanite slave.
phrases.notes: 'There' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows a woman to buy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by type of slave)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a woman to buy every kind of male slave, so he argues with our ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows only an עבד כנעני. Everyone agrees a woman may not buy an עבד עברי.

steps.title: Why an עבד עברי is a bigger concern than an עבד כנעני
steps.stepSummary: An עבד עברי would keep things private for her, so there is a real risk of sin. An עבד כנעני would not keep things private, so she will stay away from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עבד עברי is discreet toward her; an עבד כנעני is indiscreet toward her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the distinction in step 19. It shows why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can allow an עבד כנעני but not an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about צניעות. A woman might trust an עבד עברי to keep a sin secret, and that makes sinning more likely. An עבד כנעני would spread the story, so she would be afraid and hold herself back.

keyTerms.meaning: Indiscreet, does not keep things private

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean an עבד כנעני is more proper. It means his lack of discretion acts as a check, so the risk of sin is actually smaller with him.
steps.whatToRemember: A גר can own an עבד עברי only under the rules of a gentile owner, so the slave does not pass to his children. A woman cannot buy an עבד עברי, and even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, because he allowed only an עבד כנעני.

phrases.english: A Hebrew slave is discreet toward her,
a Canaanite slave is indiscreet toward her.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶבֶד עִבְרִי צְנִיעַ לַהּ, עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי פְּרִיץ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the distinction made in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern is greater with an עבד עברי because he would keep a sin secret, while an עבד כנעני would expose it.

steps.title: Why can a widow not raise a dog?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reasoning of Step 20 using רב יוסף's teaching that an אלמנה may not raise a dog. A dog would follow her around and expose her, so she should be too afraid to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב יוסף taught: A widow should not raise a dog, and she should not let a Torah student stay as a lodger in her home. The student makes sense, because he keeps things private for her. But a dog? Since it would follow her around afterward, she would be afraid to sin with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions a teaching of רב יוסף. Using the logic of Step 20, a dog that would follow her around should scare her away from sin, so why is it forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20 the rule was this: if something would expose her, she will stay away from sin. A dog that follows her around would expose her, just like an עבד כנעני who does not keep things private. So the ban on a dog seems to go against that logic. The ban on a Torah student is no problem, because he is discreet.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah student (literally, 'a son of the house of the Rebbe')
Lodging; staying as a guest in someone's home

phrases.english: But this that Rav Yosef teaches:
A widow may not raise a dog,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא תַּשְׁרֵי בַּר בֵּי רַב בְּאוּשְׁפִּיזָא.
phrases.english: and she may not let a Torah student stay as a lodger.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בַּר בֵּי רַב צְנִיעַ לַהּ,
phrases.english: Granted, a Torah student is discreet for her,
but a dog,
since it would follow her around, she is afraid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'exposure stops sin' logic of Step 20 to the dog case and finds a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ban on a widow raising a dog
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If anything that would expose her keeps her from sin, a dog that follows her around should keep her from sin too, so it should be allowed.

steps.title: People will blame the meat
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a dog also follows a woman who throws it meat. People will say the dog follows her for the food, so it does not really expose her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: A dog also follows her when she throws it a piece of meat. So people will say: It is following her because of the meat she threw it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the dog. The dog's following her would not make anyone suspicious, so it does not scare her away from sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 20 still stands: exposure keeps her from sin. The answer is that a dog does not really expose her, because people have an innocent explanation for its behavior. So the ban on raising a dog fits the logic after all.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי שָׁדְיָא לֵיהּ אוּמְצָא
phrases.english: They say: Since when she throws it a piece of meat
it follows after her,
people will say:
Because of the meat that she threw it,
that is why it follows her.
phrases.notes: Nobody will suspect anything, so she is not scared off from sinning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי שָׁדְיָא לֵיהּ אוּמְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the dog's behavior has an innocent explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dog following her would expose her, just like an עבד כנעני.
steps.terutzMaskana: People will think the dog follows her for food, so there is no exposure and the ban stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is about real exposure. Something only keeps her from sin if people would actually become suspicious. A dog does not do this, because people will blame the meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion of the woman and the עבד, and shows that the 'fear of exposure' logic depends on how people will actually react.

steps.title: Can you take interest from a גר תושב?
steps.stepSummary: A new difficulty: the פסוק seems to forbid taking רבית from a גר תושב. But the משנה says you may borrow from and lend to a גר תושב with interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty about the גר תושב mentioned regarding interest? It is written: 'And if your brother becomes poor and his means fail with you, you shall strengthen him, a stranger and a resident, and he shall live with you. Do not take interest or increase from him, and fear your God, and let your brother live with you.' And this contradicts the משנה: One may borrow from them and lend to them with interest, and the same is true with a גר תושב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second part of רבי's puzzle from step 11: the גר תושב mentioned regarding רבית. It quotes a פסוק that seems to forbid interest from a גר תושב, then points out that the משנה allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a stranger and a resident' right before 'do not take interest from him.' This makes it sound like the ban on רבית covers a גר תושב. But the משנה clearly says a גר תושב is treated like a non-Jew, so interest is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who lives in the Land of Israel and accepts the seven Noahide laws, but has not fully converted
Two words the תורה uses for interest
And they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָאָמוּר לְעִנְיַן רִבִּית מַאי הִיא,
phrases.english: The ger toshav mentioned regarding interest, what is it?
As it is written: 'And if your brother becomes poor,'
'and his means fail with you,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶחֱזַקְתָּ בּוֹ גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב וָחַי עִמָּךְ.
phrases.english: 'you shall strengthen him, a stranger and a resident, and he shall live with you.'
'Do not take interest or increase from him,'
'and fear your God, and let your brother live with you.'
And this contradicts: One may borrow from them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means non-Jews, in our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַלְוִין אוֹתָן בְּרִבִּית, וְכֵן בְּגֵר תּוֹשָׁב!
phrases.english: and lend to them with interest, and the same with a ger toshav!

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָאָמוּר לְעִנְיַן רִבִּית מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the woman and the slave and goes back to the second half of רבי's puzzle from step 11, the גר תושב regarding רבית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that interest is allowed with a גר תושב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק mentions 'a stranger and a resident' right before forbidding interest 'from him,' which suggests interest from a גר תושב is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: A גר תושב is NOT a full convert. He keeps the Noahide laws but is not Jewish, which is why the משנה can treat him like a non-Jew for רבית.

steps.title: 'From him' means from a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the פסוק says 'from him' in the singular, not 'from them.' It refers only to a Jew, so a גר תושב is not included in the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Is it written 'do not take from them'? It is written 'from him,' meaning from a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the contradiction by reading the פסוק carefully. The ban on interest is only about a Jewish borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban covered both the brother and the גר תושב, the פסוק would say 'from them' in the plural. Since it says 'from him' in the singular, it means only 'your brother,' the Jew. So the משנה is right that interest is allowed with a גר תושב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (a way of saying the פסוק does not say that)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Is it written 'do not take from them'?
'From him' is written, meaning from a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק (singular versus plural)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on interest in the פסוק covers the גר תושב too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From him' is singular and refers only to a Jew, so interest from a גר תושב is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on רבית is about a Jewish borrower. A גר תושב, like any non-Jew, may be lent to and borrowed from with interest.

steps.title: You may be a guarantor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the same words of the פסוק: you may not take interest from him, but you may become a guarantor for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Do not take interest or increase from him.' But you may become a guarantor for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns a limit from the same words of the פסוק. Taking interest is forbidden, but being a guarantor is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'do not take.' From this wording the ברייתא learns that becoming a guarantor 'for him' is allowed. It does not yet say in which case this applies, and the גמרא defines that more exactly on the next amud. This sets up a new rule about interest.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor; someone who promises to pay if the borrower does not

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אַל תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית״ –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'Do not take interest or increase from him,'
but you may become a guarantor for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same words of the פסוק discussed in Steps 23–24 to teach a new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking interest is forbidden, but becoming a guarantor in an interest deal is permitted.
